title: RAG Evaluation Is Broken! Here's Why (And How to Fix It) - Yuval Belfer and Niv Granot
talk_summary: Speakers argue RAG benchmarks are broken because they use local synthetic Q&A and test retrieval or generation in isolation, not messy end-to-end behavior. They show standard RAG fails aggregative questions on a 22-document FIFA corpus and propose structured ingestion into a SQL schema for suitable corpora, while noting normalization and ambiguity limits.

takeaways.what_they_do: They criticize benchmarks built from local questions with local answers and retrieval-only or generation-only tests, because they miss parsing, chunking, and messy real queries. They recommend evaluating the whole pipeline on realistic data.
takeaways.evidence_quote: There's also not a holistic way to test the entire system
takeaways.numbers: 22-document FIFA corpus; standard RAG pipelines scored 5% and 11% correct on aggregative questions

takeaways.what_they_do: They describe a vicious cycle: teams optimize for flawed benchmarks, celebrate high scores, then fail on customer data and create new flawed benchmarks. They recommend grounding evaluation in real-world behavior.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we're building a rug system for flawed benchmarks because you have to optimize for something

takeaways.what_they_do: For homogeneous corpora with relational questions, they cluster documents, infer a schema, populate it per document, and answer queries via text-to-SQL instead of top-k chunk retrieval. They note this does not fit every corpus.
takeaways.evidence_quote: take this unstructured corpus and convert it into a data structure and then ask the question on top of this data structure
takeaways.numbers: Standard RAG scored 5% and 11% correct on their aggregative FIFA questions

takeaways.what_they_do: They split work so heavy compute happens during ingestion and inference stays fast, mirroring regular RAG flow but with schema population done ahead of time.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you invest the compute in the ingestion and you try to do things quickly in the inference

takeaways.what_they_do: They show normalization problems like West Germany vs Germany and scalar-vs-list host countries, plus ambiguity when users ask about entities outside the schema. They flag this as an ingestion and inference issue.
takeaways.evidence_quote: normalization is an issue both during the ingestion and inference
